chunks: And that which indicates the second category is what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Zur'ah from Abu Basir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sacrificial animal of the Nāsib (one who is hostile to the Imams) is not permissible.'

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: The Nāsib, a technical term for one who is hostile or opposed to the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams
key_terms.ذَبِيحَةُ: Sacrificial animal / meat offered in the name of God

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from a Nāsib according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the impermissibility of consuming meat slaughtered by the *Nāsib* (specifically the Khawarij or early anti-Alid sects), linking dietary purity to theological allegiance. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that the religious identity and orthodoxy of the slaughterer (*dhakī*) directly impact the validity of the sacrifice, distinguishing them from the *Ahl al-Kitab* whose meat is generally permitted.
